dialogue.content: こんにちは
dialogue.English: Hello.

dialogue.content: (こんにちは)(宜しくお願いします)
dialogue.English: (Hello.) (Thank you for seeing me.)

dialogue.content: よろしくお願いいたします
dialogue.English: I look forward to working with you.

dialogue.content: 少し早いですが始めますか？時間どおりの方が良いですか？
dialogue.English: It's a little early. Shall we begin, or would you prefer to start at the scheduled time?

dialogue.content: (はじめても大丈夫です)
dialogue.English: (It's fine to start now.)

dialogue.content: はい、ありがとうございます。ではよろしくお願いいたします。
dialogue.English: Alright, thank you. Let's get started then.

dialogue.content: こんにちは相談員ですよろしくお願いいたします
dialogue.English: Hello, I'm your counselor. Thank you for coming in today.

dialogue.content: こんにちは。宜しくお願いします。
dialogue.English: Hello. Thank you for your time.

dialogue.content: 今日はどのようなご相談でしょうか？
dialogue.English: What would you like to talk about today?

dialogue.content: はい。夫の事で相談がありました。
dialogue.English: Yes. I wanted to talk about my husband.

dialogue.content: 夫さんとの事でいらっしゃいますね
dialogue.English: I see, it's about your husband.

dialogue.content: もう少し詳しくお聞かせ願えますか？
dialogue.English: Could you tell me a little more about it?

dialogue.content: はい。私は今、65歳で夫はひとつ年上なんですが、最初、行動がおかしくて、認知症ではないかと、、、
dialogue.English: Yes. I’m 65 now, and my husband is a year older. At first, his behavior seemed strange, and I wondered if it might be dementia...

dialogue.content: 66歳の夫さんの行動が最近、お気になりはじめたのですね
dialogue.English: So you've recently started to become concerned about your 66-year-old husband's behavior.

dialogue.content: はい。脳神経内科を受診したのですが
dialogue.English: Yes. We saw a neurologist, but...

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: 現段階でははっきりとした認知症ではないと診断されたのですが
dialogue.English: At this stage, he wasn't diagnosed with definite dementia, however.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: 去年、退職してから
dialogue.English: Since he retired last year,

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: Mm-hm.

dialogue.content: 散歩中に転んでしまい
dialogue.English: he fell while out for a walk,

dialogue.content: 転倒なさってしまったのですか
dialogue.English: He had a fall?

dialogue.content: はい、大腿部を骨折して、しばらく入院したあたりから少し様子が変なんです。
dialogue.English: Yes, he fractured his femur and was hospitalized for a while. Around that time, he started to seem a bit different.

dialogue.content: それは大変ご心配でいらっしゃいますよね
dialogue.English: That must be very worrying for you.

dialogue.content: 他には
dialogue.English: And besides that,

dialogue.content: どんな事がご心配になられておられますか？
dialogue.English: what else has been concerning you?

dialogue.content: はい。それまで夫は大変活動的で
dialogue.English: Well, until then, my husband was very active,

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: アウトドア派で
dialogue.English: the outdoorsy type,

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Right.

dialogue.content: 山菜採りに出かけたり
dialogue.English: he would go foraging for wild edible plants,

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: Mm-hm.

dialogue.content: 前向きで明るい性格だったのですが、転倒して骨折したあたりから急に弱気になり
dialogue.English: He used to have a positive and cheerful personality, but since he fell and fractured his bone, he's suddenly become timid,

dialogue.content: うちに籠るようになっただけでなく
dialogue.English: and not only has he started to shut himself in at home,

dialogue.content: おんなじことを繰り返し繰り返し言ったり
dialogue.English: but he also repeats the same things over and over,

dialogue.content: 車の運転も危なっかしいことがあり、
dialogue.English: and his driving has become dangerous at times,

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: 前の夫とはまるで別人のようになってしまったんですね。
dialogue.English: He's become like a completely different person from the husband I knew before.

dialogue.content: それで
dialogue.English: And so...

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね
dialogue.English: I see, so that's what happened.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: それで
dialogue.English: And so...

dialogue.content: 夫さんも活動的な方が故に
dialogue.English: Being such an active person,

dialogue.content: 骨折とご入院でさぞご不安になられたでしょうね
dialogue.English: the fracture and hospitalization must have made him feel very anxious.

dialogue.content: そうだったのだと思います。
dialogue.English: I think so, too.

dialogue.content: ごめんなさい、お話しさえぎってしまいました
dialogue.English: I'm sorry, I interrupted you.

dialogue.content: 大丈夫です。もともと本人は病院が大嫌いでしたが娘に説得され脳神経内科に受診し、認知症の検査をしたのですが、まだ現段階では認知症とは診断されなかったのです。
dialogue.English: It's alright. He's always hated hospitals, but our daughter persuaded him to see a neurologist and get tested for dementia. But, as I mentioned, he wasn't diagnosed with dementia at this stage.

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね一気に色々な事が重なりご不安もつのりますね
dialogue.English: I see. With so many things happening all at once, it's natural for your anxiety to grow.

dialogue.content: はい。そうなんです。前の夫とはまるで性格が変わってしまっただけでなくあんなにしっかりしていた人なのに、、、財布をどこにしまったか忘れてしまったり、、、
dialogue.English: Yes, that's right. Not only has his personality completely changed, but he used to be so on top of things... and now he forgets where he put his wallet...

dialogue.content: 急に起こり出したりして
dialogue.English: and he suddenly gets angry,

dialogue.content: まだまだこれからを楽しみにしていたのに、ショックが大きくて、、、
dialogue.English: I was so looking forward to our future together, so this has been a huge shock...

dialogue.content: 夫さんが退職をなさってから、骨折をなさってご入院となり、言動も以前とは変わられてしまいさぞご心配も並大抵ではまいですよね
dialogue.English: After your husband retired, he fractured his bone and was hospitalized, and now his words and behavior have changed—your worries must be immense.

dialogue.content: そうなんです。
dialogue.English: It is.

dialogue.content: そうですよねショックはでてしまって当然のことですよね
dialogue.English: Yes, it's completely natural to feel shocked.

dialogue.content: 本当に誰にどう相談したら良いのか、、、こんな不安な気持ちになるなんて、
dialogue.English: I really didn't know who to talk to or what to do... I never imagined I'd feel this anxious.

dialogue.content: しっかりなさっていらした夫さんの性格変貌や忘れ物など認知症かもとご心配になりますよね
dialogue.English: Seeing your once-capable husband's personality change and his forgetfulness, it's understandable that you'd worry it might be dementia.

dialogue.content: そうですよね
dialogue.English: Of course.

dialogue.content: そうなんです。はい。
dialogue.English: Yes, exactly.

dialogue.content: それで市の高齢福祉課に相談に行ったのですが
dialogue.English: So, I went to the city's Elderly Welfare Division for advice, but...

dialogue.content: ご不安と、ご心配とショックはかなり大きい事は充分わかります
dialogue.English: I can fully understand that your anxiety, worry, and shock are quite significant.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: 高齢福祉課ではなんと？
dialogue.English: What did they say at the Elderly Welfare Division?

dialogue.content: たらい回しにされたあげくに介護保険の申請は夫よりももっともっと重度の人が優先されるからの一点張りで
dialogue.English: After being passed from one person to another, they just kept insisting that applications for long-term care insurance are prioritized for people with much more severe conditions than my husband.

dialogue.content: ええたらい回しにされてしまったのですか！
dialogue.English: What? They gave you the runaround?

dialogue.content: そうなんです。もうガッカリしてしまいました。今まで一生懸命に働いてきて介護保険料もきちんと払ってきたのに、、、
dialogue.English: Yes. I was so disappointed. We've worked hard our whole lives and properly paid our long-term care insurance premiums...

dialogue.content: 担当者の説明によると
dialogue.English: According to the person I spoke with,

dialogue.content: 重度の方が優先なのはわかりますが、困ってる事へのフォローもなかったのですね酷い！
dialogue.English: I understand that more severe cases are a priority, but to offer no follow-up for someone who is clearly struggling... that's terrible!

dialogue.content: そうなんです。長時間待たされたあげくまた同じ説明を最初から何度もさせられて、行政って縦割りとは聞いてましたがガッカリしてしまいました。
dialogue.English: Exactly. After being made to wait for a long time, I had to explain the same thing over and over from the beginning. I'd heard that government services can be bureaucratic, but I was still so disappointed.

dialogue.content: ご心配をぬぐってももらえず、あげくに酷い対応では悲しすぎましたよね
dialogue.English: To not have your concerns addressed and on top of that to be treated so poorly... that must have been heartbreaking.

dialogue.content: そうなんです。。。涙が出てきてしまいました。
dialogue.English: It was... It brought me to tears.

dialogue.content: そこで離れて暮らす娘に相談したら
dialogue.English: So I talked to my daughter, who lives separately,

dialogue.content: すがる思いでお尋ねになられたのに・・・
dialogue.English: And you went there clinging to the hope of getting help...

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: そうなんです。そしたら娘がいろいろ調べてくれて
dialogue.English: Exactly. And then my daughter did some research for me,

dialogue.content: 娘さんが知恵をしぼってくださったのですね
dialogue.English: So your daughter really put her mind to it for you.

dialogue.content: はい。地域包括ケアセンターのケアマネージャーさんに話を聞いてもらえることになり、
dialogue.English: Yes. She arranged for me to speak with a care manager at the Community Comprehensive Support Center,

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: Mm-hm.

dialogue.content: そのケアマネージャーさんに一度家庭訪問をお願いして夫の様子を見てもらったのですが
dialogue.English: and I asked the care manager to make a home visit to see how my husband was doing.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 夫はいちもよりシャンとして何にも困っていないからお引き取りくださいと、言ったので担当のケアマネージャーさんもこのまますこし様子を見ましょうと言うのです。
dialogue.English: But my husband acted sharper than usual and said, "I'm not having any trouble, so please leave." So the care manager said we should just monitor the situation for a little while.

dialogue.content: いつもよりの間違いでした。
dialogue.English: I meant 'more than usual.'

dialogue.content: そうだったのですか
dialogue.English: I see, that's what happened.

dialogue.content: 夫さんも
dialogue.English: Your husband, too,

dialogue.content: 第三者の前ではご自身を保つのに精いっぱいだったのですね
dialogue.English: must have been trying his best to keep it together in front of a stranger.

dialogue.content: でも、
dialogue.English: But...

dialogue.content: ご相談者さんとしては、困ってる状態を事実のまま把握して欲しかったですよね
dialogue.English: from your perspective, you wanted them to understand the reality of the difficult situation you're in.

dialogue.content: そうなんです。訪問の短時間だけでは全然伝わらないし、、
dialogue.English: Exactly. A short visit isn't nearly enough to convey what's happening...

dialogue.content: そうですよね！
dialogue.English: Of course it isn't!

dialogue.content: このままでは私の方が先にダメになりそうで不安です。
dialogue.English: I'm afraid that at this rate, I'll be the one to break down first.

dialogue.content: 介護は介護している側の方が一番お辛いですよね
dialogue.English: In caregiving, it's often the caregiver who suffers the most.

dialogue.content: ケアマネジャーのかたは
dialogue.English: As for the care manager,

dialogue.content: 夫さんの様子だけで、相談者さんの困りごとには寄り添ってもらえなかったのも酷いですよね
dialogue.English: it's terrible that they only focused on your husband's condition and didn't listen to your struggles.

dialogue.content: そうなんです！
dialogue.English: Exactly!

dialogue.content: なんだか
dialogue.English: I feel like...

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: Yes?

dialogue.content: 私がひとりで騒ぎ立てて神経質なタイプと思われているかも知れません。
dialogue.English: they might think I'm just an oversensitive person making a fuss over nothing.

dialogue.content: そう感じてしまわれたのですね
dialogue.English: That's how it made you feel.

dialogue.content: 本当に夫はその訪問の短時間はしっかりとシャンとするんですよ。
dialogue.English: My husband really does pull himself together and act sharp during that short visit.

dialogue.content: ええ夫さんも第三者には自分らしさをしっかりおみせになられたかったのでしょね
dialogue.English: Yes, your husband probably wanted to present his capable self to a stranger.

dialogue.content: でも
dialogue.English: But,

dialogue.content: それでは、本当の問題解決のはならないですし、何より相談者様のご不安やご心配、悲しみは消えないですよね
dialogue.English: that doesn't lead to a real solution, and more importantly, it doesn't erase your anxiety, worry, and sadness.

dialogue.content: そうなんです。ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: That's right. Thank you.

dialogue.content: 今まで本当に苦労の連続でこれから二人でやっと好きなことが楽しめる矢先だったのに、、、
dialogue.English: Our life has been a series of hardships, and we were just at the point where we could finally enjoy doing things we like together...

dialogue.content: 夫さんは、定年なさってから骨折でご入院なされ
dialogue.English: After your husband retired, he was hospitalized for a fracture,

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: その事がきっかけで、性格も変貌するときもおありになられ、物忘れも、活動的でなくなってしまったのも
dialogue.English: and that triggered a personality change, forgetfulness, and a loss of his active lifestyle.

dialogue.content: ご相談者さまとしては認知症もうたがいながらもこれからお二人のゆっくりした時間を過ごせることを楽しみになさっていたのに
dialogue.English: and for you, while you suspected it might be dementia, you had been looking forward to finally spending some peaceful time together.

dialogue.content: そうなんです……
dialogue.English: That's right...

dialogue.content: ご自身のご心配もご不安も拭えないまま今、日々ショックの感情でお過ごしという感じでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Is it fair to say that you're living day by day with this feeling of shock, unable to resolve your own worries and anxieties?

dialogue.content: そうですね。私が先に倒れてしまうのではないかと最近では思うこともあります。
dialogue.English: Yes. Lately, I sometimes find myself thinking that I might be the one to collapse first.

dialogue.content: 不眠傾向もありますし、頭痛もすごいんです。
dialogue.English: I've also been having trouble sleeping, and the headaches are terrible.

dialogue.content: 夫さんの事を心配に思いながらも相談者さんご自身まで体調まで崩されてしまわれたのですね
dialogue.English: So while worrying about your husband, your own health has begun to suffer.

dialogue.content: はい。。。
dialogue.English: Yes...

dialogue.content: 不眠や、頭痛はお辛いですね・・・
dialogue.English: Insomnia and headaches must be very difficult to deal with.

dialogue.content: はい。これから先のことを考えると余計、不安が募ります。夫は絶対に介護保険サービスを使ってデイサービスに行ったり、拒否するのはわかっています。本当に心細く感じます。
dialogue.English: Yes. When I think about the future, my anxiety just grows. I know my husband will absolutely refuse to use long-term care services like going to a day service center. I feel so helpless.

dialogue.content: 病院嫌い医者嫌い薬嫌いどうしたらいいか、、、
dialogue.English: He hates hospitals, doctors, and medicine... I don't know what to do.

dialogue.content: 夫さんも第三者の前ではプライドがおありですから拒否はされてしまうかもですね
dialogue.English: Your husband has his pride, especially in front of others, so he might refuse.

dialogue.content: でも
dialogue.English: Even so,

dialogue.content: このままでは、ご相談者さん自身が気分も体力もお疲れ過ぎて心配です
dialogue.English: I'm concerned that if things continue like this, you'll become exhausted, both emotionally and physically.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: 夫さんは
dialogue.English: As for your husband,

dialogue.content: プライドもおありでしょうから、相談者さまがご自身のゆとりのお時間や気持ちを取り戻すことが先決ですよね
dialogue.English: he has his pride, so the priority should be for you to regain some time and peace of mind for yourself.

dialogue.content: 確かに、そうですね。
dialogue.English: You're right, that makes sense.

dialogue.content: 夫からは
dialogue.English: My husband tells me,

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: Yes?

dialogue.content: お前はあんまり神経質過ぎる俺だってお前にいろいろ心配かけないように努力しているんだ。あんまりいろいろ言われると、逆にイライラする。俺は大丈夫だから絶対に介護保険サービスは受けないと、、、
dialogue.English: "You're too sensitive. I'm trying my best not to make you worry. When you keep saying things, it just irritates me. I'm fine, so I will absolutely not accept any long-term care services..."

dialogue.content: 我が家が一番だからと。
dialogue.English: He says, "Being at home is best."

dialogue.content: 夫さんからすればそうなんでしょが・・・
dialogue.English: From your husband's perspective, that may be true, but...

dialogue.content: それでは
dialogue.English: In that case,

dialogue.content: ご相談者さんが救われないままになってしまいます
dialogue.English: you won't get the relief you need.

dialogue.content: 夫さんを動かそうとするのではなく
dialogue.English: Instead of trying to change your husband's mind,

dialogue.content: はい…
dialogue.English: Yes...

dialogue.content: 相談者さまが楽になる方法を考えていきたいですね
dialogue.English: let's think about ways to make things easier for you.

dialogue.content: 先ずは
dialogue.English: First of all,

dialogue.content: あっ、ありがとうございます。なんだかそう言ってもらえて救われます。
dialogue.English: Oh, thank you. It's a relief to hear you say that.

dialogue.content: 又、ご苦労になってしまうかもしれませんが
dialogue.English: This might be difficult for you again, but

dialogue.content: ケアマネージャの方に相談者さまご自身の困っている実情を訴え、
dialogue.English: explain to the care manager the reality of the difficulties you're facing,

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Okay.

dialogue.content: ヘルパーさんなどの手をかりながら夫さんには第三者との交流になれてもらい
dialogue.English: with the help of a home helper, get your husband used to interacting with other people,

dialogue.content: 相談者さんご自身のゆったりとしたお時間をつくりことから始めてみるのは如何でしょうか？
dialogue.English: how about starting by creating some relaxed time for yourself?

dialogue.content: 後、
dialogue.English: Also,

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 娘さん以外にも相談者さまの気持ちを今日烏有出来る人材が必要ではとも思います
dialogue.English: I think you also need someone, besides your daughter, with whom you can share your feelings.

dialogue.content: 共有でした
dialogue.English: I meant 'share.'

dialogue.content: たしかに、そうですね。ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: That's true. Thank you.

dialogue.content: ケアマネージャーさんに再度コンタクト取って見ようと思います。
dialogue.English: I'll try contacting the care manager again.

dialogue.content: ご苦労になり、またがっかりしてしまわぬ様に祈るのみですが
dialogue.English: I can only hope that it won't be another difficult and disappointing experience for you,

dialogue.content: 相談者さまの良き理解者は必要だと思いますこの状態から少しでも楽になって頂きたいです
dialogue.English: but I believe you need a good support system. I truly hope you can find some relief from this situation.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。じっくり話をしてみようと思います。そして、来週あたり娘もこちらに来る用事があるようなので、相談してみます。
dialogue.English: Thank you. I'll try to have a thorough talk with them. And my daughter has plans to come here next week, so I'll talk to her about it as well.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: それはよかったです！ちょうど娘さんもお見えになられるのですね
dialogue.English: That's wonderful! It sounds like your daughter is coming at just the right time.

dialogue.content: はい。タイミングよかったです！
dialogue.English: Yes, the timing is perfect!

dialogue.content: 相談して良かったです！ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: I'm so glad I spoke with you! Thank you.

dialogue.content: では、娘さんともまた、よく話し合っていい方向にいけることを祈っております
dialogue.English: Well then, I hope that you can have a good discussion with your daughter and that things will move in a positive direction.

dialogue.content: こちらこそ、お話ししてくださりありがとうございました
dialogue.English: Thank you for sharing your story with me.

dialogue.content: 気持ちが楽になりました。ありがとうございます。お世話になりました。
dialogue.English: I feel so much lighter. Thank you for all your help.

dialogue.content: 今日は、終了となってしまいますが、いつでもまたご連絡くださいね
dialogue.English: Our time is up for today, but please feel free to contact me again anytime.

dialogue.content: はい。その際にはまたよろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: Yes, I will. Thank you again.

dialogue.content: 少しでもお役にたてたのなら嬉しい限りです
dialogue.English: I'm very happy if I was able to help even a little.

dialogue.content: 話を聞いてもらえてこんなに楽になるのですね。ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: I didn't realize how much better I'd feel just by having someone listen. Thank you.

dialogue.content: では、現状態が良き方向に行けること願っております
dialogue.English: Well then, I hope your current situation improves.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: こちらこそありがとうございました
dialogue.English: Thank you as well.

dialogue.content: それでは今日はこれで失礼いたします
dialogue.English: Alright, that's all for today. Goodbye.

dialogue.content: 失礼いたします。
dialogue.English: Goodbye.

dialogue.content: (お時間過ぎてしまいましたが最後までお付き合い頂きありがとうございました)
dialogue.English: (We've gone over our time, but thank you for staying with me until the end.)

dialogue.content: (こちらこそ、ありがとうございました！)
dialogue.English: (No, thank you!)

dialogue.content: (では、またお会いできた時はよろしくお願いいたします)
dialogue.English: (Well then, I look forward to speaking with you again.)

dialogue.content: (こちらこそ！ありがとうございました！
dialogue.English: (Likewise! Thank you very much!)

dialogue.content: (これで終了で大丈夫ですか？)
dialogue.English: (Is it okay to end here?)

dialogue.content: (はい！ありがとうございました
dialogue.English: (Yes! Thank you very much.)

dialogue.content: (ありがとうございます。では、失礼いたします)
dialogue.English: (Thank you. Goodbye, then.)

dialogue.content: (ありがとうございました。失礼いたします
dialogue.English: (Thank you very much. Goodbye.)
